title: Add template CLI: initial `init` command for scaffolding quickstarts
author: Monica Patel
description: This PR adds the first slice of the quickstart scaffolding CLI: `init`. The goal is to let users scaffold a chosen quickstart template from a single command while we iterate on the template portfolio and release/versioning story. Scope intentionally stays minimal (no upgrades, no doctor, no deploy) but establishes the structure we’ll build on in follow-up PRs. What `init` does: (1) selects a template (via `--template` flag; if omitted, prints a short list + instructions), (2) copies the template directory into a target output folder, (3) applies light templating for project name/package name placeholders, (4) writes a version stamp file so support + docs can identify the originating CLI/template version, (5) prints next steps (env vars, install deps, run). Version stamping: writes `.redwood-template.json` with `template_id`, `template_version`, `cli_version`, and `generated_at` (no secrets; no user data). This is meant to support troubleshooting and future upgrade workflows (we can detect “generated by CLI vX”). Template resolution: for now, templates are sourced from the repo at build time (bundled in the published CLI package). This keeps UX simple and avoids needing network access during init. We can revisit remote template resolution once we have a stable registry/versioning policy. UX details: supports `--dir` (defaults to current directory), `--force` to allow non-empty dirs (with a loud warning), and `--yes` to skip confirmation. Error messages aim to be actionable (e.g., if target dir exists, if template ID is unknown, if placeholder substitution fails). Non-goals: do not attempt to install deps, do not validate API keys, do not configure OTel collector, and do not add telemetry. Follow-ups: `doctor` command (ENG-4185 follow-up / PR-111), docs updates to point to CLI install, and a release workflow to publish CLI versions alongside template releases.
commits_summary: 1) chore(cli): add package skeleton + build configuration 2) feat(cli): implement `init` command (copy + placeholder replacement) 3) feat(cli): add version stamp `.redwood-template.json` + constants for template IDs 4) test(cli): add unit tests for init (dir handling, unknown template, force) 5) docs(cli): add README usage + examples; wire into repo root docs
changed_files: Added: cli/package.json, cli/tsconfig.json, cli/src/index.ts, cli/src/commands/init.ts, cli/src/templates/index.ts, cli/src/lib/copy.ts, cli/src/lib/replace.ts, cli/src/lib/stamp.ts, cli/src/lib/validate.ts, cli/test/init.test.ts, cli/README.md. Updated: root README to mention CLI (internal for now), template scaffolds to use standardized placeholders for project/package name.
implementation_notes: The CLI is implemented in TypeScript (Node 18+) and published as a single package with a `bin` entry (current name: `@redwoodinference/quickstart-cli`, subject to final naming). Template copy uses a conservative allowlist approach: copies the selected template directory, excludes node_modules/.venv/.git, preserves executable bits, and avoids following symlinks. Placeholder replacement is intentionally small: `{{PROJECT_NAME}}`, `{{PACKAGE_NAME}}`, `{{APP_SLUG}}`. We avoid attempting to mutate arbitrary code beyond these markers to keep diffs predictable and maintenance low. Version stamp file example: `{ "template_id": "rag-agent-python", "template_version": "0.1.0", "cli_version": "0.1.0", "generated_at": "2025-02-24T18:12:03.221Z" }`.
cli_usage_examples:
Install (dev): `pnpm --filter @redwoodinference/quickstart-cli build` then `node cli/dist/index.js init --template rag-agent-python --dir ./my-app`.
Planned (published): `npx @redwoodinference/quickstart-cli init --template rag-agent-python --dir ./my-app`.
Flags: `--template <id>`, `--dir <path>`, `--force`, `--yes`.
review_conversation: Dana Lo: Can we ensure `--force` doesn’t silently overwrite files? I’d prefer we hard-fail unless `--force` is passed, and even then refuse to overwrite existing files by default. Monica Patel: Updated behavior: if dir is non-empty and `--force` is set, we still refuse to overwrite conflicting files and print a list of conflicts + suggested remediation (choose empty dir / delete conflicts). Connor O'Brien: Version stamp file name + schema: please align with future release tooling; also prefer a stable key for template ID (no human-friendly display name). Monica Patel: Switched to `.redwood-template.json` and `template_id` string constants; version fields match semver strings. Sahana Iyer: Tests look good but we should cover Windows path separators and ensure copy doesn’t follow symlinks. Monica Patel: Added a test for path normalization and explicitly disabled symlink following in copy helper; added a CI note for Windows runner in follow-ups. Elliot Price: README output should include next steps and point to docs once ready; avoid mentioning internal-only env vars. Monica Patel: Adjusted `init` final output to only mention required env var name (`REDWOOD_API_KEY`) and a generic link placeholder for docs (to be updated when docs PR lands). Dana Lo (follow-up): Please keep template IDs consistent between CLI and repo folder names. Monica Patel: Added `templates/index.ts` mapping and a check that folder exists at build time; mismatch causes build failure. Approvals: Dana Lo approved after conflict behavior change; Sahana Iyer approved after test additions; Connor O'Brien approved with note to revisit package naming before public launch.
ci_checks: pnpm lint (pass), pnpm test (pass), pnpm build (pass), package-size (pass). Initial run failed on lint due to unused import in `stamp.ts`; fixed in follow-up commit and reran CI.
release_notes: Internal: Adds the initial quickstart scaffolding CLI `init` command. Enables generating a quickstart app from a template and writes a `.redwood-template.json` version stamp for supportability.
